title: The angels
hookLine: Jibril who brings revelation, Mika'il, Israfil, the recorders on each shoulder

lines: TURN RIGHT: PEACE BE UPON YOU.
cards: Watch the end of a Muslim prayer. After the last sitting, the person praying turns their head to the right and says, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Then to the left, the same words.
If they're praying alone in an empty room, they still turn. Who are they greeting? Partly the people beside them, if there are any.
And, some scholars say, someone who's always there: the angels. Today, the mala'ikah.

teach.b: Mala'ikah is the plural; one angel is a malak. Some lexicons link it to a root for sending a message, and surah thirty-five opens by calling the angels messengers, with wings, two, three and four.
A hadith in Sahih Muslim says they were created from light. In the hadith of Jibril, also in Sahih Muslim, belief in them is one of the pillars of faith. A few are named.

Jibril, Gabriel, brings the revelation down; al-Baqarah, verse ninety-seven, names him as the one who brought it to the heart of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Mika'il, Michael, is named once, in the very next verse.
Tradition connects him with rain and provision.

Israfil isn't named in the Qur'an at all: the Qur'an speaks of the trumpet that will be blown on the last Day, and the hadith tradition gives the angel of the trumpet the name Israfil. Then the ones closest to daily life.

teach.h: ONE ON THE RIGHT, ONE ON THE LEFT.
teach.b: Surah fifty says two receivers sit, one on the right and one on the left, and not a word is spoken without a watcher ready. Surah eighty-two calls them kiraman katibin: noble ones, writing, who know what you do.
Some scholars teach that the one on the right records the good, and the one on the left the bad.

teach.h: A GOOD INTENTION IS WRITTEN TOO.
teach.b: And a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim says that when someone intends a good deed and doesn't do it, it's still written as one good deed. Intending a bad one and holding back is written as a good deed too.
The ones who write, it turns out, are generous with the pen.

how: Muslims count belief in angels among the pillars of faith; at the end of each prayer they turn the head to the right and then the left with the greeting of peace, which some scholars say includes the angels.

o: the jinn, made of smokeless fire
the souls of the righteous after death

s: Israfil is named in the Qur'an
the Qur'an mentions the trumpet; the name Israfil comes from the hadith tradition.
a good deed intended but not done is still written
a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim says it counts as one good deed.
the Qur'an describes angels with wings
surah thirty-five: wings, two, three and four.

games.q: you meant to call a sick friend today, and the day ran out. according to the hadith, what do the writers on your right record?
o: one good deed, for the intention.
games.why: the hadith says a good intention not carried out is written as one good deed; carried out, it's multiplied.

practice: Sit upright and turn your head gently to the right; if you'd like, say the words of the prayer's end, as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah, or let the greeting be silent. Then turn to the left and do the same.
Sit with the thought that a good intention counts, even the ones you didn't finish.

wordCard.voice: Mala'ikah. Angels, messengers of light: Jibril with revelation, Mika'il, Israfil with the trumpet, and the noble writers on the right and left. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the ones who write. Even an unfinished good intention goes in the record. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 8 (the hadith of Jibril: belief in the angels)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6491; Sahih Muslim 131 (good intentions recorded)
